questions.q: What is the blue hat used for?
a: Managing the thinking process and the session
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls it the hat for thinking about thinking.

questions.q: Who usually keeps the blue hat on for the whole meeting?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the facilitator keeps it on to enforce the rules.

questions.q: What happens under the red hat?
a: People state feelings without explanation or judgement
People list facts and figures in order
People vote on the strongest option
questions.why: Lesson 2 says emotions are voiced freely and nobody has to justify them.

questions.q: Why does the summary say the red hat matters?
a: It keeps resentment out of the final solution
It reveals which facts are missing
questions.why: Lesson 2 says airing feelings prevents grudges from carrying into the solution.

questions.q: What does the yellow hat encourage?
a: Realistic optimism about an idea's potential value
Cautious criticism of every new idea
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the yellow hat as value-sensitive optimism grounded in reality.
